items.title: Litigants can file applications in Kannada before Administrative Tribunal: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that litigants can file pleadings, including applications, in Kannada before the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal (KAT) [ Suryakanth v. KPSC ]. A Division Bench of Justice Ashok S Kinagi and Justice Subramanya Rangarao passed the ruling while setting aside a June 2025 KAT order that had rejected a Kannada-language application filed by one Suryakanth. The Court held that applications fall within the meaning of “pleadings” under Rule 9(iii) of the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal Rules of Practice, 1990, which expressly permits pleadings and other documents to be filed in either English or Kannada. The Bench concluded that there is no prohibition on litigants filing applications in Kannada before the tribunal. "There is no complete embargo on the part of the litigants to file an application in Kannada. The parties can file an application in Kannada in terms of Rule 9(iii) of 1990 Rules and the 1986 Rules provides that the Bench, in its discretion, may permit the use of Kannada in the proceedings, subject to the condition that the final order should be in English," the October 7 ruling explained. items.title: Kavin caste killing: SC upholds quashing of chargesheet against accused’s cop parents
items.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal by the Tamil Nadu Crime Branch Crime Investigation Department (CB-CID) challenging a Madras High Court order to quash the chargesheet against two accused in the honour killing of Dalit techie C Kavin Selvaganesh. In September, the Madras High Court had quashed the chargesheet against the first accused, Surjith’s parents, Saravanan and Krishnakumari, both of whom are police officers. According to reports, the apex court has also criticised the state government's handling of the case. Kavin was hacked to death on July 27, 2025, at Tirunelveli’s KTC Nagar. He hailed from Arumugamangalam in Thoothukudi district and was in a relationship with a Thevar woman (Other Backward Class). Surjith, her brother, allegedly killed Kavin because he opposed the inter-caste relationship. The case was transferred to the CB-CID after it emerged that Surjith’s parents, Saravanan and Krishnakumari, were police officers and were named as accused. Both are sub-inspectors in the Tamil Nadu Special Police Force and were suspended from service following the murder. items.title: Umar Khalid moves Supreme Court seeking bail in Delhi riots conspiracy case
items.summary: Former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) scholar and Delhi riots conspiracy case accused Umar Khalid has moved the Supreme Court seeking bail in the case. He has challenged the September 30 order of the Delhi High Court denying him bail. The Delhi High Court had observed that the Supreme Court had denied bail to Khalid and Imam in January 2026, stating that they can file for bail again after a year or after the protected witnesses have been examined. The High Court said that since the two conditions have not been met yet, granting bail to Khalid and Imam would amount to modifying the Supreme Court order, which the High Court cannot do. “In view of the above discussion and overall facts of these cases, specifically the conditions imposed by the Supreme Court in Gulfisha Fatima, this court cannot find fault with the order passed by the trial court. The present appeals are therefore dismissed,” the court said. This is the second time Khalid is approaching the Supreme Court seeking bail. items.title: Delhi High Court questions itself for entertaining IP cases with trivial links to Delhi; warns of jurisdiction ‘Lakshman Rekha’
items.summary: The Delhi High Court, a preferred forum for Intellectual Property (IP) disputes, has now questioned the practice of litigants filing IP suits before it based on the most insignificant connection with the national capital [ABD Maestro Private Limited v Great Galleon Ventures Ltd + Connected matters] . In a 246-page judgment delivered on November 3, Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav also took a dim view of the High Court entertaining such IP suits despite having little connection to the national capital. The Court acknowledged that India’s IP landscape has largely grown under the “Banyan Tree” of the Delhi High Court. But the judge cautioned that this Banyan Tree must not stunt the growth of other trees below it. “India’s IP landscape to a large extent has grown under the Banyan Tree, which is the Delhi High Court. While the Banyan provides shelter and comfort, it also stunts the growth of other trees below it. There is no reason to believe that other High Courts will not rise to the occasion, create a specialised machinery like this Court, and make IP litigation conducive either before them, or the district courts,” the Court said. items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court quashes FIR against journalist over report on Ganesh Visarjan procession violence
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently quashed a criminal case against a journalist accused of promoting enmity through a news report on an incident of violence during a Ganesh Visarjan procession in 2025 [Uvesh Khan @ Uvesh Reporter vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh] Justice Himanshu Joshi said that mere reporting of an incident involving violence does not constitute the offence of promoting enmity or disharmony between different groups under Section 196(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). "The nature and content of the publication, the context in which it was made, and the requisite connection with the promotion or attempted promotion of enmity between groups are material considerations," the Court said. It added that the freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution cannot be curtailed merely because a report concerns a sensitive public incident. Any restriction on such expression must be justified in law, the bench said.
